question.problem:
The function $f(x)=\frac{2}{3}-{5}^{2x-k}$ has an inverse function given by 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{2}{log}_{5}⁡(\frac{2-3x}{3}).
$$

What is the value of $k?$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{2}{3}-{5}^{2x-k}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{2}{3}-{5}^{2y-k}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{2}{3}-{5}^{2y-k} \\ {5}^{2y-k} & =\frac{2}{3}-x \\ {5}^{2y-k} & =\frac{2-3x}{3} \\ {log}_{5}⁡({5}^{2y-k}) & ={log}_{5}⁡(\frac{2-3x}{3}) \\ 2y-k & ={log}_{5}⁡(\frac{2-3x}{3}) \\ 2y & ={log}_{5}⁡(\frac{2-3x}{3})+k \\ y & =\frac{1}{2}{log}_{5}⁡(\frac{2-3x}{3})+\frac{k}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{2}{log}_{5}⁡(\frac{2-3x}{3})+\frac{k}{2}$  

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=0.$
